extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, PD/PIs, sponsors, and institutional grants administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Policies and procedural requirements for preparing, submitting, and post-submitting NIH grant applications, including eRA Commons registration, application types, NOFO requirements, resubmission rules, post-submission materials, and PI/organizational assurances.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons PI role and responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Designating the PI role in the eRA Commons provides the individual with the administrative authority needed to see pertinent information regarding an application (e.g., summary statements, scores, electronic submission status, etc.) and is necessary to complete the grant application process and post-award actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PD/PI may delegate certain authorities to other individuals. The PI role (and SO role) can view impact score and summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain personal eRA Commons profile
rubrics_metrics.description: After the initial registration process is complete, it becomes the responsibility of each individual to maintain the information in their personal profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals must verify that all Personal Information in the Personal Profile tab is accurate; required fields vary by role for NIH reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single PD/PI eRA Commons account
rubrics_metrics.description: Users should only have one PD/PI eRA Commons account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If already registered in eRA Commons by another organization, separate registration with the submitting organization is not necessary but the submitting organization must affiliate the individual so they can view/access records.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons registration for undergrad/grad/postdoc participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual with an Undergraduate, Graduate Student, and/or Postdoctoral Role who participates in a NIH-funded project for at least one person month or more should be registered in the eRA Commons and should verify that all Personal Information is accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This registration is required regardless of whether salary is charged to the project; Commons ID for these roles is not required at submission but is required for the RPPR (post-award).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required data items for trainee roles
rubrics_metrics.description: When assigned Undergraduate, Graduate Student, or Postdoctoral Role, responses to certain data items in the Personal Profile tab will be required to meet NIH reporting requirements to Congress (NIH Reform Act, P.L. 109-482).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For postdoctoral level, progress reports will not be accepted if the Commons ID is not provided; recipients are encouraged to begin registering undergrad/grad roles now.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role restrictions for fellowships and training grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduate Student and Postdoctoral eRA Commons Roles should NOT be used for individuals submitting Individual Fellowships; the PD/PI role is used for those submissions. They also should not be used for individuals supported on institutional training grants and reported using xTrain; the Trainee Role must continue to be used for those individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commons ID required at submission for specified roles
rubrics_metrics.description: A Commons ID is required at the time of submission for sponsors in fellowship applications, component leads on multi-project applications, primary mentors on career development applications, and all individuals listed on the R & R Senior / Key Person Profile (Expanded) Form, including Other Significant Contributors (OSCs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For other roles a Commons ID is strongly encouraged but optional; a general Commons Role of Project Personnel is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of application (competing and non-competing) - definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Five application types commonly used: New Application (Type 1), Renewal (Type 2), Competitive Revision (Type 3), Administrative Supplement (Type 3.), Resubmission (suffix -A1), and Non-Competing Continuation Progress Report (Type 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each type has specific purposes, review requirements, and submission constraints (e.g., administrative supplements do not require peer review; resubmissions require prior summary statement and only one resubmission is allowed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application (white paper) usage
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH periodically uses a pre-application to facilitate certain approaches, often in a 2-phase process; pre-applications do not result in an award but may allow submission to a subsequent phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also used for permission to access NIH research resources; pre-applications generally do not award funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: NOFO as umbrella term and requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: NOFO (Notice of Funding Opportunity) is a publicly available document outlining program goals, eligibility, and application requirements; all applications must be electronically submitted in response to a NOFO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOFO types include Program Announcements (PAs, including Parent Announcements) and Requests for Applications (RFAs); application must be associated with a specific NOFO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parent Announcement use
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent announcements (omnibus/umbrella) are provided for applicants to submit investigator-initiated (unsolicited) applications to ensure correct application packages and enable NIH to receive applications from Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parent announcements are NIH-wide but some ICs may limit participation; check announcement for IC participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Announcement (PA) characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: A PA is a formal statement about a new or ongoing extramural activity or program; it may serve as a reminder of interest, describe modifications, or invite applications and is normally reviewed with standard peer review processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH may use PARs (PAs with special receipt/referral/review considerations) and PASs (PAs with set-aside funds); PARs/PASs may list non-responsive criteria in the Funding Opportunity Description (Part 2, Section 1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for Applications (RFA) characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: An RFA solicits grant or cooperative agreement applications in a well-defined scientific area to accomplish specific program objectives and indicates set-aside funds, estimated number of awards, cost-sharing, and submission dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RFAs usually are reviewed by an SRG specially convened by the awarding component; for cooperative agreements, RFAs describe responsibilities of NIH and recipients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trials NOFO requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications involving one or more clinical trials must be submitted through a NOFO specifically designed for clinical trials; NIH will not process applications proposing clinical trials if the NOFO indicates clinical trials are 'Not Allowed.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications with mixed trial and non-trial aims must be submitted to NOFOs designated as clinical trial 'Optional' or 'Required.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal implications and AOR certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The signature of an Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) certifies that the organization will comply with all applicable assurances and certifications; the applicant organization is responsible for verifying conformity with most current guidelines and for appropriate oversight and accountability for funds and performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will not accept forms/documentation bearing generic departmental signatures; all forms must reflect the name of the individual with institutional authority to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with federal, state, and local requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants and recipients are responsible for and must adhere to all applicable Federal statutes, regulations, and policies (including income tax regulations) and are expected to be in compliance with applicable State and local laws and ordinances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions about tax applicability should be directed to the IRS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of eligibility and public policy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may be required to provide proof of organizational eligibility, trainee/fellow eligibility and citizenship, or other eligibility information; applications must demonstrate compliance (or intent to comply) with public policy requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant public policy requirements for peer review include human subjects protections, inclusion policies, and live vertebrate animal research compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical application contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Application information typically includes a project description, budget and budget justification, biographical sketches of senior/key personnel, and other information specified in the application instructions, announcement, or program guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult cost principles and general administrative requirements for their organizational type when preparing budgets and other parts of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct cost limit policy excluding consortium/contractual indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: For NOFOs that include a direct cost limit, NIH policy excludes consortium/contractual indirect costs when determining compliance with the direct cost limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy applies to all solicited and investigator-initiated applications and affects eligibility for modular budgets (used for requests of $250,000 or less in direct costs per year); consortium indirect costs may be requested in addition to the $250,000 direct cost limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission of unfunded RFA applications — when to submit as new
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless a NOFO permits resubmissions from an RFA, unfunded applications should be submitted as new applications if they fall into specified categories (originally submitted to an RFA, originally investigator-initiated then submitted to an RFA, or originally one activity code then submitted as another).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new application must follow new application instructions and must not include an Introduction describing changes or reference prior review; reviewers will not be provided the previous summary statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission (A1) policies for unfunded applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An unfunded competing application (A0) may be resubmitted as a resubmission application (A1); NIH will accept only a single resubmission (A1) application. NIH will accept a new (A0) application after an unsuccessful resubmission (A1) or prior A0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subsequent new applications need not demonstrate substantial changes in direction but must not contain an Introduction responding to prior critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlapping applications policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH will not accept duplicate or highly overlapping applications under review at the same time, including: (1) a new A0 submitted before issuance of the summary statement from review of an overlapping A0/A1, (2) an A1 submitted before issuance of summary statement from previous A0, and (3) an application substantially overlapping another application pending appeal of initial peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37-month window for one resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH policy allows a 37 month window for one resubmission (A1) following the submission of a new, renewal, or revision application (A0). After 37 months, NIH views a submission as a new application regardless of prior A1 submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The initial submission of the A0 establishes the start of the 37-month window.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Investigator and Early Stage Investigator (ESI) definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: A New Investigator has not previously competed successfully as PD/PI for a substantial NIH independent research award. An ESI is a New Investigator within 10 years of completing terminal research degree or end of post-graduate clinical training and who has not competed successfully as PD/PI for a substantial NIH independent research award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of ESI eligibility may be requested per NIH procedures; ESI status is determined from eRA Commons profile data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review expectations for New Investigators and ESIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer reviewers will be instructed to focus more on the proposed approach than track record for New Investigators and ESIs and to expect less preliminary data than for established investigators; New Investigator applications may be clustered during review and given special consideration at funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH intends to support New Investigators at success rates comparable to established investigators; ESIs should comprise a majority of New Investigators supported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program Director/Principal Investigator assurance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant organizations must secure and retain a unique signature and dated assurance from the PD/PI for each submitted application certifying (at least) that: (1) information is true, complete and accurate; (2) false statements may subject the PI to penalties; and (3) the PI accepts responsibility for scientific conduct and required progress reports. If multiple PIs, assurance must be retained for all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For individual Fellowship applications, the assurance requirement applies to both the Fellow and the Sponsor with additional sponsor-specific certifications (see below).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellow/Sponsor assurance certifications
rubrics_metrics.description: For individual Fellowship applications, assurance must include: (1) that information submitted is true, complete and accurate; (2) that false statements may subject Fellow and Sponsor to penalties; (3) that the Sponsor will provide appropriate training, adequate facilities, and supervision; (4) that the Fellow has read and will abide by the Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA Payback Assurance if awarded; and (5) that the award will not support residency training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All forms must reflect the name of the individual with appropriate institutional authority; NIH will not accept generic departmental signatures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission materials general policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-submission of application materials is not required and NIH will only accept materials after initial submission but prior to initial peer review if resulting from unforeseen administrative issues; adding materials may be counterproductive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy does not modify Just-in-Time or other post-peer review information requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable post-submission materials for all applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable materials include citations of issued patents; revised budget page(s); biographical sketches (due to hiring/replacement/loss); letters of support/collaboration (due to hiring/replacement/loss); adjustments from natural disasters; adjustments from change of institution; news of professional promotion or tenure decisions; approval by NIH Stem Cell Registry of a human embryonic cell line after submission; video/audio files (within defined limits) that demonstrate devices/experimental data with temporal elements; other materials specified in the NOFO or special Guide Notice; and news of an article accepted for publication limited to list of authors, title, and journal/citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of articles, links, or other materials related to accepted articles are not accepted unless specified in the NOFO or special Guide Notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional post-submission materials for certain application types
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain application types may accept extra post-submission items: Preliminary data for Type 1 R01/R21/R03 if NOFO allows; training grant updates (trainee graduation/employment/promotion/funding/publications, faculty promotions/funding/publications, addition/removal of faculty, lists of publications for T32 with page limits); Individual Fellowship (F) and Career Development (K) allowed items like new Sponsor/Mentor funding info (limited to project title, source, brief aims and relevance) and news of change in Mentor(s) or Senior/Key Persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference grants (R13, U13) may submit one-page explanations of speakers accepted/declined or a one-page explanation per plenary slot; RFAs accept the same post-submission materials as other applications; other types of post-submission materials are unlikely to be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and page limit requirements for post-submission materials
rubrics_metrics.description: All post-submission materials must conform to NIH policies on font size, margins, and paper size as referenced in applicable application instructions; specified formats and page limits apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not on a specific format page and no specified page limit exists, each explanation or letter is limited to one page; if the application has multiple components each subproject or core is allowed explanations/letters but each is limited to one page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for post-submission materials to SRO
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-submission materials must be received by the NIH Scientific Review Officer (SRO) no later than 30 calendar days prior to the peer review meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials will not be accepted if fewer than 30 calendar days remain before the peer review meeting unless NOFO or special Guide Notice states otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: AOR concurrence for post-submission materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Concurrence from the Authorized Organization Representative (AOR) of the applicant organization is required for post-submission materials; AOR must send materials directly to the SRO or send concurrence to the PD/PI who will forward materials and concurrence to the SRO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A communication from the PD/PI only, or with a copy to the AOR, will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and transmission of post-submission materials (PDF/video)
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-submission materials can only be submitted as a PDF attachment, except for video submissions which have special procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SRO is responsible for uploading acceptable materials into the official electronic grant file maintained in eRA Commons; PD/PI can check their application in the Commons section titled 'Additions for Review'.
